extracted.intended_audience: Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) personnel, airport/aircraft firefighters, and first responders tasked with 787 incidents
extracted.subtask_description: Recommended firefighting tactics and procedures for responding to lithium-ion battery events in the Boeing 787 electrical and electronic (E&E) bays, including venting, suppression, PPE, and handover to maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment of battery failure
rubrics_metrics.description: A battery failure reaction should be fully contained within the stainless steel enclosure with any gasses vented overboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reinforced stainless steel enclosure is capable of containing a lithium-ion battery event; venting of vapor may be visible from an exterior vent on the bottom of the airplane under the forward or aft E&E bay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passenger and crew safety / evacuation expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Passengers and crew are safe inside the airplane. Passenger evacuation is not expected for a battery failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While passengers/crew are generally safe inside, responders must still follow exterior evacuation guidance (see exterior evacuation distance) and monitor the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior evacuation distance and upwind placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evacuate area around exterior of the airplane upwind to at least 18m/60 ft. from airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move people upwind to minimize exposure to any hazardous vapors vented overboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not access E&E bay during active venting
rubrics_metrics.description: While venting, make no attempt to access E&E bay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During active venting there is no reason to make access to the E&E bay; wait until venting has ceased and atmosphere is clear before entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm airplane electrical power shutdown prior to access
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm airplane power is shut down by communicating with the flight deck prior to making access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not access E&E bay until positive confirmation from flight deck that aircraft power is shut down to reduce electrical hazard risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal protective equipment and hot zone distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Don all fire fighting Personal Protective Equipment including Self Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) when entering the Hot Zone (9m/30 ft).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full PPE including SCBA is required for anyone entering within 9 m / 30 ft of the airplane (Hot Zone) to protect from heat and hazardous vapors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when venting is complete or not occurring
rubrics_metrics.description: If battery is not venting or venting is complete, access the E&E bay to ensure there is no other visible fire source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after venting is complete should responders check the E&E bay for other fire sources; follow suppression sequence if flame is visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression agent selection
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of visible flame Halon (or Halon replacement) is the recommended agent to suppress a fire. If Halon, or Halon replacement is unavailable, then CO2 would be the recommended agent. Do not use dry chemical or powder of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer agents that suppress without introducing powders or residues that can exacerbate electrical/chemical hazards. Explicit prohibition against dry chemical/powder is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood-and-seal suppression sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Flood the E&E bay with appropriate agent for approximately 20 to 30 seconds and then close the bay hatch for at least 60 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After flooding and sealing, open the hatch to confirm fire is out. If flame is present repeat the flood-and-seal step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat suppression until fire confirmed extinguished
rubrics_metrics.description: Open E&E hatch to confirm fire is out. If flame is present repeat step #7b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue flood-and-seal cycles until there is no visible flame when the hatch is opened for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disconnect or cut battery connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Make no attempt to disconnect the battery pack from the airplane’s electrical system using the quick disconnect or by cutting the battery cables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts to disconnect or sever battery connections can cause electrical arcing, further damage, or escalate chemical reactions and are strictly forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature monitoring of reinforced box
rubrics_metrics.description: Use heat detecting equipment to monitor temperature of reinforced box. Temperatures may reach as high as 338 degrees Celsius/640 degrees Fahrenheit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor external box temperature to guide decisions about continued response actions and when it is safe to hand over to maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handover criteria to maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the external temperature of the reinforced box is below 49 degrees Celsius/120 degrees Fahrenheit and atmosphere is clear of hazardous vapors, then the airplane can be turned over to maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both temperature and atmosphere clearance are required before turnover; document conditions and communicate status to maintenance personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize pressure burst disc indicator status
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressure Burst Disc Indicator — Actuated / Not Actuated (main battery and APU battery indicators are the same).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual check of the pressure burst disc indicator can help determine whether a pressure relief event has occurred; use indicator status along with visible venting to assess the event.
